items.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 27 at 3:36PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend. 1-3 more inches of precipitation
are expected by the end of the week which will keep water levels
high.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 27 at 3:00PM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Southeast winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 55 mph
expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Southeast winds will become strong and gusty
by Tuesday night. Winds are expected to be strongest along the
coast. Winds will begin to diminish Wednesday morning.
items.areas: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
items.instruction: Winds this strong can make travel difficult. Use extra caution.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 2:20PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
into Tuesday have caused portions of that snowfall to melt,
creating many slushy areas of melting snow and pooling water.
Overnight low temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning
are expected to fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will
allow much of this slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very
